label: Thursday evening, the landau pulls up at a red-brick villa

labels.label: Thursday evening, the landau pulls up at a red-brick villa
Thursday evening, the landau pulls up at Straker's villa

quote: A few minutes later our driver pulled up at a neat little red-brick villa
note: Holmes sits on in the carriage, absorbed, until Watson touches his arm (¶69–70). The talk with Gregory and the Colonel at the door follows (¶71–77).

label: Thursday evening, Straker's pocket things laid out in the sitting-room
quote: We all filed into the front room and sat round the central table
note: Gregory opens the tin box. The knife, the papers and the milliner's account are examined (¶78–85).

label: Thursday evening, Mrs. Straker in the passage
quote: As we emerged from the sitting-room a woman, who had been waiting in the passage
note: Holmes asks about the garden-party at Plymouth (¶86–92).

label: When Straker's body was brought back to his house
note: Holmes's 'Straker was brought back here, I presume?' (¶72). Not otherwise dated. The things from his pockets go into Gregory's tin box at some time after the body was found.

label: When Mrs. Straker told the Inspector of the knife and of Derbyshire
quote: His wife tells us that the knife had lain upon the dressing-table
note: Also told in ¶84: 'Mrs. Straker tells us that Derbyshire was a friend of her husband's'. This was before Holmes arrived; it is not otherwise dated.

label: The times when letters for William Derbyshire were addressed to Straker's house
quote: occasionally his letters were addressed here
note: This is what Mrs. Straker says. It is undated and in the past.

label: When Madame Lesurier made out the account to William Derbyshire
quote: a milliner’s account for thirty-seven pounds fifteen made out by Madame Lesurier, of Bond Street, to William Derbyshire
note: The text does not date it. The account was in Straker's pocket at his death, so it comes before the crime, but the text does not order it against that point.

label: Some little time ago, a garden-party in Plymouth
quote: Surely I met you in Plymouth at a garden-party some little time ago
note: This is Holmes's claim, and Mrs. Straker denies it (¶90). The dove-coloured silk costume belongs to this claim (¶91–92).
